note.text: A useful rule names the setting, the action and whether it is required or prohibited. Keep one main instruction in each statement. Use must or must not consistently, or an appropriate imperative. Rules should be clear, respectful and practical rather than vague threats. Explain a purpose where it helps. A set of classroom rules needs consistent presentation and should not pretend to be an official policy unless the school has approved it.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A useful rule names the setting, the action and whether it is required or prohibited. Keep one main instruction in each statement. Use must or must not consistently, or an appropriate imperative. Rules should be clear, respectful and practical rather than vague threats. Explain a purpose where it helps. A set of classroom rules needs consistent presentation and should not pretend to be an official policy unless the school has approved it.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Library rules: Return borrowed books by the agreed date. Keep food away from the books. Speak quietly so others can read. Ask the librarian before moving reference materials.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Plan the behaviours first. Turn each into a clear instruction and check that positive and negative wording match the intended meaning. Read the set for contradictions. The exercise creates a draft in an exercise book, not a new school policy.
